quote: He didn't tell me. He said, it was, a grant or something that the state pays. Not me in the state. He said it take four to six months to get approved.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior conversation (with an unnamed 'he') about a 'grant' with a 4-6 month approval window — almost certainly a garbled reference to the federal tax credit. The rep never asks who this was (another Ion rep? a different company?) or corrects the 'grant' framing, letting a live misconception ride to the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this was too deep a rabbit hole for a setter call and deliberately left it for the closer to unpack with full context. But the rep never even names it as a tax credit or flags it for the appointment — it's punted silently, not deliberately staged.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 10 seconds clarifying: 'who talked to you about that, and was it Ion or another company?' — this is free competitive intel and also lets the rep correct the 'grant' misconception before it compounds by Friday.

quote: Oh, yes. A single family home. This is me and my wife.
stewart_read: Customer names his wife as a co-occupant of the home unprompted, but the rep never asks if she's on the title or should be included in the Friday appointment. Later the wife's medical appointment ('gotta take my wife to a hard doctor') surfaces as the reason tomorrow doesn't work — meaning she has her own schedule and was never confirmed for Friday at 10.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have assumed 'me and my wife' plus 'we got the furnace fixed' implies joint decision-making is understood and doesn't need restating. But nothing in the transcript confirms she'll actually be present Friday.
coaching_implication: This is a concrete, missable protocol gap: the rep should have asked 'will your wife be able to join us Friday at 10?' The appointment is booked without confirming the co-decider will attend, which risks a stalled close per protocols.spouse_decision guidance that setters who skip this step create structurally vulnerable appointments.

quote: Oh, wow. Yeah. That is a big deal.

coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add one line after the acknowledgment tying the number to the appointment's purpose — e.g., referencing that the design Friday will show exactly how much of that $350-400 gets eliminated.

Flagging as a borderline case: the deferral is correct procedure, but it comes without ever correcting the 'grant' misconception first.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a clean example of holding scope rather than a miss — the rep does NOT attempt to explain tax credit mechanics himself, which is the right instinct per the universal escape hatch.
coaching_implication: Praise the boundary-holding instinct, but pair it with the earlier coaching note: hold scope AND correct the factual misconception ('that's actually a federal tax credit, not a state grant — the specialist will explain exactly how it works Friday') rather than passing the wrong framing forward untouched.
